sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Giant's Causeway is an Irish mythological site. It is a series of massive basalt columns that form steps out to sea. The formation lies near Portrush in County Coleraine, in the province of Ulster. Folklore credits giant builders with its creation. In one tale Fionn mac Cumhaill bested the Scottish giant who built the step-shaped rocks as the start of an invasion of Ireland.

okr.objective: Document the Giant's Causeway as an Irish mythological site with geological and legendary layers.
key_results: Establish the Giant's Causeway as a Place-typed site
Record the basalt column formation and Ulster location
Record the folklore of giant builders and Fionn mac Cumhaill
